I have farmed long enough to know I should not spread myself too thin, but I also should not put all 42 mu into one kind of crop. I will keep the wheat-maize rotation as the backbone of my land because that is the most steady system for my area, and I have well irrigation so I can support grain production in a dry spell. I will still keep some cotton because it fits my experience and spreads risk, but I will not let cotton take too much land because returns can swing and picking takes labor. I will plant cucumber on a smaller area because it needs more water, fertilizer, spraying, and closer daily attention, but it brings cash if I manage it carefully. For seed, I will use better seed where it matters because I want stable emergence and yield. For fertilizer, I will feed wheat and maize steadily, give cucumber the heaviest input because it is a high-demand crop, and give cotton more potassium to hold bolls better. For irrigation, I will rely on my well and water the grain crops at key stages, while cucumber gets the most frequent water. For tillage, I will keep operations simple and practical: rotary tillage for most fields and no-tillage maize after wheat where it saves time and keeps the season moving. What I want this year is steady grain, some cash income from cucumber, and risk control from keeping cotton in the mix.
